Mr. Khandaker Mahbubuddin Ahmed with Mr. Mirza Hossain Haider, Advocates ----- For the Petitioners. 
Dr. M Zahir with Mr. M Hassan, Mr. Ferdousi Shahab and Mr. Firoz Shah, Advocates ----- For the Respondent Nos. 1 and 2 .
Mr. Rafiqul Huq, Attorney-General with Mr. AY Salehuzzaman, Deputy Attorney-General ----- For the added Respondent No. 4.

parties:
Sattar Match Works and others ----- Petitioners
Vs.
Bangladesh Chemical Industries Corporation and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
2. Before considering the case of the parties let me narrate the history of the case which ultimately has given rise to the present dispute between the parties. As back as in the year 1953 one Abdul Sattar Ahmed and Begum Ashrafunessa Khaton established a Match Factory at Shympur, District Dhaka in the name of "Sattar Match Works" and in the year 1954 the said Sattar Match Works had registered the "Cock" brand as Trade Mark under the Trade Marks Act, 1940, for its safety matches, and started using this trade mark Cock on its match boxes. The Trade Mark was numbered as 21785 in the Registry of Trade Marks in Class 34. In the year 1962 the owners of Sattar Match Works established another match factory it Lama, Chittagong Hill Tracts, which was also named as "Salim Match Works" and which being under the same management also used the same trade mark "Cock" on its match boxes. The two factories under the same owners carried on their business under the name of "Sattar Match Works" for some time and thereafter the owners constituted themselves into a private limited company under the Companies Act, 1913, by the name of "Pakistan Manufacturers and Industries Limited" and ownership of Sattar Match Works at Shyampur, Dhaka and at Lama, Chittagong Hill Tracts, vested in the said Company. In the year 1964 Pakistan Manufacturers and Industries Limited purchased "Ujala Match Factory", situated at Chota Katra, Dhaka, in an auction sale by the liquidator under an order of this Court and the machineries of the said Ujala Match Factory were removed from its original site to Shyampur, in 1965 in the same premises of Sattar Match Works. In the year 1968 Sattar Match Works at Shyampur, Dhaka was renamed by the said company as "Ujala Match Factory". After the plant and machineries of Ujala Match Factory were amalgamated with the Sattar Match Works at Shyampur, Dhaka, the company was running its factory Sattar Match Works at Lama and Ujala Match Factory at Shyampur, with the same trade mark "Cock" on its match boxes. In this way the aforesaid company had been running its business of both the match factories, one as Ujala Match Factory at Shyampur and the other as Sattar Match Works at Lama with the same Trade Mark "Cock'. 

 3. After liberation of Bangladesh the Ujala Match Factory at Shyampur, Dhaka and Sattar Match Works at Lama, Chittagong Hill Tract as well as the Pakistan Manufacturers and Industries Limited were taken over and vested in the Government as abandoned property under the Presidential Order No. 16 of 1972. After taking over the management of the aforesaid 2 Units the same were placed under the erstwhile Bangladesh Fertilizer Chemical and Pharmaceutical Corporation (BFCP Corporation) under the provisions of PO 27 of 1972 and subsequently the BFCP Corporation along with 2 other Corporations were amalgamated and named as Bangladesh Chemical Industries Corporation (BCIC) under Ordinance 25 of 1976. 

 6. It was required by Article 6 that application for summary registration must be filed within 1 year from the date of commencement of this order dated 15.3.73. At the relevant time both the match factories being abandoned properties were being managed and run by the Administrators of the Government. The Administrator of Ujala Match Factory at Shyampur filed an application for summary registration on 4.4.73 having No. 1294 in class-34 for trade mark "Cock". The Administrator of Sattar Match Works at Lama also filed an application for summary registration on 11.4.73 having No. 1354 in class-34 before the Registrar, Trade Marks for summary registration of the trade marks "Cock" on the match box. Upto the year 1978 summary registration was not given either to Ujala Match Factory or to the Sattar Match Works. On 13.10.78 the Sattar Match Works at Lama was sold by the Government and the same was purchased by the petitioner No. 2 as per deed of agreement dated 13.10. 78. On 23.11.79 the BCIC trading as Bangladesh Manufacturers and Industries Limited got the registration of trade mark "Cock" by serial No. 1294 in class 34. On 13.12.79 this registration was given to BCIC trading as Bangladesh Manufacturers and Industries Limited for 15 years with effect from 1976 regarding the Trade Mark "Cock" by serial No. 1294 in Class 34. Under an order of the Government dated 2.7.80 the company M/s Bangladesh Manufacturers and Industries Limited was wound up on the terms that all assets and liabilities of Bangladesh Manufactures and Industries Limited Dhaka were taken over by the M/S Ujala Match Factory, Shyampur, Dhaka and that management of Bangladesh Manufacturers and Industries Limited shall be merged with Ujala match Factory, Shyampur, Dhaka. After the winding up of the aforesaid company the registration was amended to the effect that henceforth Bangladesh Chemical Industries Corporation trading as Bangladesh Manufacturers and Industries Limited would be read as Bangladesh Chemical Industries Corporation trading as Ujala Match Factory, Shyampur, Dhaka. 

 7. In the year 1986 the BCIC and Ujala Match Factory as plaintiffs instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 12 of 1986 against the Bhaiya Group of Industries, the purchaser of Sattar Match Works at Lama and the Sattar Match Works having its factory premises at Aziz Nagar, PS Lama, Chittagong. Hill Tracts for permanent injunction and for restraining the defendants and their employees and agents and authorised dealers and distributors from using the safety matches and label containing the device of "Cock", Ultimately the Additional District Judge-in-charge, Dhaka, granted temporary Injunction restraining the defendants from using the trade marks "Cock" on their match boxes till the disposal of the suit. Thereafter, in 1988 the present petitioners namely, the owners of Sattar Match Works, Bhaiya Group of Industries filed the present application for rectification of the registration in the office of the Registrar Trade Mark by deleting the Trade Mark "Cock" from the register which was given to the Ujala Match Works under No. 1294 in Class 34. 

 8. In the above back ground of this case the present application has been moved before this Court with a prayer for rectification of the register of Trade Mark as stated above. It is stated in the application that since 1954 the Sattar Match Works had been using this trade mark "Cock" on the match boxes produced in that match factory. This trade mark was used in the Sattar Match Works at Shyampur as well as at Sattar Match Works at Lama. Before liberation this Ujala as well as Sattar were using this trade mark "Cock" as because before liberation both the units belonged to the same company and after the creation of Bangladesh Government took over the two Industrial Units under PO No. 16 of 1972. It is stated that only after the injunction order was passed by the District Judge in 1986 the petitioners were restrained from using the aforesaid trade mark "Cock" but not before that. 

 10. An affidavit-in-opposition has been filed on behalf of the Respondent No. 3, the Registrar of Trade Marks. He has annexed photo copies of certain office records vide annexures 1 and 1(a)-1(g). The petitioner also filed an affidavit-in-reply to the affidavit-in-opposition of the respondent No. 3. Further the petitioner has submitted a supplementary affidavit with annexure 'C' showing the schedule B (A) of Raw Materials, Chemicals, Finished products and work in process of M/S Sattar Match Works and schedule B(B) of stores and spares of Sattar Match Works as verified by the inventory committee during the period from 31.3.78 to 10.6.78. 

 11. In view of the aforesaid affidavits and the papers as produced before this Court, Mr. Khandaker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, the learned Advocate, submits that when the Sattar Match Works was sold and purchased by the petitioners, the petitioners purchased all assets and properties of Sattar Match Works including its trade name, trade mark, good will etc. and as such they are entitled to get this Trade Mark "Cock". In support of his contention Mr. Khandaker Mahbubuddin has referred to the deed of agreement for sale dated 13.10.78. He submits that in the preamble it is stated that whereas the seller agreed to sell to the purchaser for a total consideration of Tk. 80,000,111.00 the Industrial unit M/S Sattar Match Works located at Amin Nagar P.S. Lama, Chittagong Hill Tracts, having its principal Office at 89, Korbaniganj, Chittagong, together with existing assets and liabilities as fully described in the schedule 1 hereunder collectively termed as demised property. He has also referred to part No. 1 of page 5 of the agreement wherein it has been agreed that the value of stock and stores as per joint inventory dated 26.6.78 is Tk. 33,38,779.67 and the commercial liabilities as on the date of agreement are taka nil as per schedule 2 annexed herein the correctness of which both the parties admitted. By an explanation "Stock and Stores "included spares, raw materials, finished products and materials at any stage of manufacturing purposes. In the supplementary affidavit annexurc 'C' at page 5 of schedule B(A) has shown at bottom the Godown RG 1 contains Match Brand Double Gun (full size) Gross, Match Brand Cock (full size) Gross, Match Brand Cock (Half size) Gross. In the last page of schedule B(B) it appears that the Cock 1/2 size Box, the Cock 1/2 size dozen and Cock 1/2 size gross were also included. At page 5 of schedule B(A) vide serial No. 9 and 15 it appears that, Match Brand Cock (full size) and Match Brand Cock (Half size) were included in the schedule. 

 12. Mr. Khandaker submits that when industrial unit Sattar Match Works was sold with all its assets and properties, the good will and trade mark 'Cock' being property of the industrial unit were also included in the category of property of the unit. He further submits that from the deed of agreement for sale along with the schedules as mentioned above it becomes quite clear that the industrial unit Sattar Match Works was purchased by the petitioners along with all its assets and properties including the good will and trade mark 'Cock'. 

 13. Dr. Zahir, on the other hand, submits that neither in the agreement for sale nor in the schedules of properties nor in the inventory it has been specifically mentioned that the goodwill and trade mark are also included in the schedule and the same has been transferred to the purchaser. Since there was no specific provision made either in the agreement with schedules or in the inventory for selling the good will and trade mark with the industrial unit Sattar Match Works, the goodwill and trade marks were not sold to the purchaser. It is difficult to accept the above contention of Dr. Zahir. If the facts and circumstances and the recitals and terms of the agreement as well as the schedules along with the inventory which formed part of the agreement are considered together, it appears to me that the industrial unit Sattar Match Works was sold along with all its assets and properties including its goodwill and trade mark 'Cock'. 

 16. Mr. Khandaker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, the learned Advocate on the other hand, submits that it is a fraud out and out committed by BCIC as well as by the Registrar of Trade Marks. He submits that these 2 industrial units belonged to the Bangladesh Manufacturers and Industries limited and BCIC was actually managing the affairs of the company as well as of the 2 industrial units. So it was incumbent upon BCIC to get the trade mark Cock in favour Sattar Match Works. It is true that under law BCIC was required to obtain the trade mark 'Cock' for Sattar Match Works. But, since this unit was sold in the year 1978 and purchased by the petitioners, BCIC lost its interest in getting the above trade mark for Sattar Match Works. Here I do not find any fraud in the action of BCIC Mr. Khandaker Mahbubuddin further submits that the fraud was also committed by the Registrar of Trade Marks inasmuch as since 1973 these two (2) applications were pending, one for the Samar Match Works and the other for the Ujala Match Factory, for the same Cock Brand. Without considering the application of Sattar Match Works, which was filed within time, the Registrar granted registration of trade mark Cock in favour of the Ujala Match Factory. In this regard also I do not find any element of fraud on the part the Registrar of trade marks. It may be called negligence or carelessness in performing his official duty, but it does not mean that Registrar committed fraud in this matter. Since the clement of fraud could not be established, I find that the submission of Mr. Khandaker has no substance. 

 18. The above sub-section (2) is very important, in my opinion, for the purpose of this case. Continuous honest and concurrent user for a long time of a trade mark is a special circumstance which warrant consideration of a case specially under sub-section (2). In order to consider this sub-Section let me repeat some of the facts already stated above. It is not disputed that Sattar Match Works at Shyampur had been using this Cock brand since 1954. It is also not disputed that when the Sattar Match Works was established at Lama in 1962, trade mark Cock was being used with its match boxes since then. When Ujala Match Factory was removed and set up at Shyampur in the premises of Sattar Match Works, it started using the trade mark Cock simultaneously with Sattar Match Works at Lama. Both the Match- factories at Lama and Shyampur under the ownership of Bangladesh (Pakistan) Manufacturers and Industries had been undisputedly using the trade mark Cock with their match boxes. Before and after creation of Bangladesh the above two industrial units had been simultaneously using the trade mark Cock without any objection whatsoever. When PO 19 of 1973 came into force one Administrator for Ujala Match Factory filed an application for summary registration for the trade mark "Cock" and another Administrator of Sattar Match Works at Lama also filed an application for summary registration for having the trade mark "Cock". Even after filing these 2 (two) applications by 2(two) separate Administrators these 2(two) match factories had been using the same trade mark "Cock" on their match boxes. The unit Sattar Match Works was sold to the present petitioners in the year 1978. After purchasing the same the petitioners were also using continuously the same Trade Mark "Cock". In the year 1979 when the summary registration was given in favour of BCIC trading as Bangladesh Manufacturer and Industries Limited, the Ujala Match Factory started using the trade mark "Cock" under new registration and when the registration was corrected in 1980 in favour of Ujala Match Factory, both the above two match factories used the same trade mark "Cock". It is the case of the petitioners that though the formal summary registration was not given to them yet they were using the same trade mark "Cock" along with the Ujala Match Factory. They used the same althrough and at no point of time this Ujala Match Factory or BCIC took any objection to it. Even after 1980 till 1986, the petitioners were using the same trade mark Cock on their match boxes along with Ujala Match Factory and there was no dispute or objection from any quarter. Only the dispute arose in the year 1986 when the suit was filed by BCIC and Ujala Match Factory against the Sattar Match Works. Fact remains that since 1954 the Sattar Match Works at Shyampur and since 1962 the Sattar Match Works at Lama, Chittagong Hill Tracts, had been using continuously and without any break the trade mark "Cock" on their match boxes. No question arose till 1986. 

 20. Dr. Zahir submits that this Court can give direction to the Registrar to dispose of the application of Sattar Match Works under section 10 of the Act, and granting of concurrent use of one trade mark by two different persons is absolutely within the discretionary power of the Registrar. Since no prayer to that effect is made in the application, this Court should not give any further relief beyond the prayer of the petitioners. This Court is fully conscious of the power given under section 10 of the Act to the Registrar. Since this Court is in seisin of the entire records of the case, it can pass such just and equitable order or orders as it deems fit and necessary in order to render substantial justice to the parties. 

 21. Under PO No. 19 of 1973 application for summary registration was filed on 11.4.73 by the Administrator of Sattar Match Works. After purchasing the Unit the present petitioners also filed an application with prescribed fee on 11.10.79 for registration of trade mark 'Cock' in their favour. On the direction of this Court, the Respondent No. 3 the Registrar Trade Marks filed an affidavit-in-opposition and produced the entire records of the case before this Court. From the records it appears that the Registrar, Trade Marks had only kept the application dated 11.4.73 of Sattar Match Works in the bundle of applications. But no step was taken nor any proceeding was started over this application. The Registrar sat over the matter for last 16 years without touching it even after filing the application by the petitioners on 11.10.79. It speaks of gross negligence, carelessness and fault of the Registrar in performing and discharging his official duty. The Registrar ought to have disposed of the matter by exercising his discretionary power as provided under section 10(2) of the Trade Marks Act, read with Article 5 of PO 19 of 1973. For such long negligence, carelessness and neglect of duty on the part of the Registrar, he forfeited his legal obligation in exercising his discretion under the above law. Since the petitioners have acquired a right to use trade mark 'Cock' and get summary registration for the same under Article 5 of PO 19 of 1973 by concurrent and honest user of the same for such a long time of about 3 decades along with Ujala Match Factory, I am of the view that this court, in order to do complete, adequate and substantial justice, should exercise its inherent discretionary jurisdiction in this particular case by giving direction to the Registrar Respondent No. 3 to grant summary registration to the petitioners for the trade mark 'Cock'. 

 22. Further, application for Sattar Match Works was filed before the Registrar in time as per provision of PO 19 of 1973. The previous registration certificate of trade mark Cock which was issued in 1954 in favour of Abdul Sattar Ahmed and his wife for Sattar Match Works is also found in the records produced by the Registrar. Requirement of summary registration under Article 5 of PO 19 of 1973 was fulfilled. Learned Deputy Attorney-General Mr. Ahmed has taken objection that there is no endorsement of payment of fee for Tk. 50.00 on the application. Even if it was not paid then, now it can be paid since the application has not yet been disposed of by the Registrar. In a case like this, non-payment of Tk. 50 as fee will not disentitle the petitioners from having summary registration of their trade mark. Since the Sattar Match Works filed application in time on 11.4.73 and the original registration certificate of 1954 is on records, I find that requirements of PO 19 of 1973 have been fulfilled and thereby Sattar Match Works acquired a vested right to get summary registration of the trade mark 'Cock' and the Registrar Respondent No. 3 is under legal obligation to accord summary registration of the trade mark 'Cock' in favour of Satter Match Works under Article 5(3) of PO 19 of 1973. Accordingly, respondent No. 3 the Registrar, Trade Marks, Bangladesh, is directed to accord summary registration of trade mark 'Cock' to the petitioners after obtaining the registration fee of Tk. 50.00 if required, without any prejudice to Ujala Match Factory for its concurrent use of the same trade mark 'Cock' with Sattar Match Works.
